input.quote: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
input.rationale: The Term runs eight years, and our only convenience exit (11.1) requires a full year's notice plus a fee measured against the Estimated Remaining Value (all remaining months at the Monthly Base Fee or recent average fees, per p0039), payable 50/50, plus uncapped unamortized Conversion costs and Expenses. That fails the fallback on two material terms: notice far exceeds 60-90 days and the early-termination charge far exceeds three months' fees. On the vendor side, 10.2 lets M&I withdraw any non-Core Services "at any time" mid-term, which is a vendor convenience right that the fallback confines to the end of a term (its 90 days' notice already meets the notice floor). We target the fallback rather than preferred because zeroing the fee would require collateral rewrites to 11.2(A) and the 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement. Noted but not flagged: p0181 (immediate withdrawal on a regulatory determination) is condition-based rather than convenience, and p0125 (EFT services) is triggered by loss of network access.

proposal.summary: Customer convenience termination on 90 days' notice with fee capped at three months' Fees; M&I service withdrawal limited to end of Term
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened our convenience notice from one year to ninety (90) days and capped the Termination for Convenience Fee at three months' Fees (deleting the additional uncapped cost pass-through), and we limited M&I's withdrawal of Services to the end of the then-current Term on its existing ninety (90) days' notice. This reflects our fallback termination-for-convenience position.

ops.oldText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
ops.newText: Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount not to exceed three (3) months' Fees.

ops.oldText: In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, any unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer.
M&I may, at any time, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)
ops.newText: M&I may, effective only at the end of the then-current Term, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services)
